title: Rav Idi bar Avin (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav Papa’s student, citing [Chullin 131a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.131a.11), where he raised an objection to Rav Papa. Hyman places him alongside Rav Ashi on the basis of the Ra’avad’s Sefer HaKabbalah. And what we find in [Chullin 141b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.141b.7), “Rav Idi said to Rav Ashi,” Hyman suggests may read Rav Idi bar Avin.

Hyman says he succeeded to Rav Ashi’s seat and cites the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4: Rav Ashi died in 738, after him Mareimar in 743, and after him Rav Idi bar Avin, who died in 763 — that is, he headed the academy in Sura twenty years.

Hyman infers from this that he lived long, since Rav Papa died in 687; even if he was then only about twenty, he lived ninety-six years. And what we find in [Niddah 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.67b.6), “Rav Idi instituted [ritual] immersion in Naresh on the eighth day” (and in Halakhot Gedolot, Hilkhot Niddah, it explains Rav Idi bar Avin), is because he was head of the academy in Sura, and Naresh is a town near Sura, as explained in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 3.[^3]

notes.text: The supplied738/743/763/687 dates remain without an invented era. Hyman’s twenty years in office and ninety-six years of life are retained with the underlying arithmetic and attributed chronology; the possible Idi identification stays tentative.

Chullin 131a directly has Idi bar Avin objecting to Rav Papa. The proposed Idi identification, the Epistle and Sefer HaKabbalah chronology, twenty-year term and ninety-six-year calculation remain Hyman’s account. The supplied years are retained without assigning an era.

The consulted passage in the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.108) gives 738, 743 and 763 but reads Rav Yemar between Rav Ashi and Rav Idi bar Avin, where Hyman writes Mareimar. The numbers are left in their source form. Niddah names Rav Idi without a patronymic and gives lions as the local reason for the ruling. Hyman’s identification and academy explanation remain his.
